Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and a straight line slants upward, intersecting the left side of the x-axis at point C and intersecting the positive half-axis of the y-axis at point D respectively; the inverse proportional function curve is in the first quadrant, and the straight line intersects the curve at point P; from P, draw a perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot of perpendicular A, and A is on the positive half-axis of the x-axis.

Reasoning: The straight line is y=kx+2, so its intersection point with the y-axis is D=(0,2), that is, OD=2. It is known that S_{△COD}=1, and △COD is a right triangle with CO and OD as the right-angle sides, therefore 1=(1/2)·CO·OD=(1/2)·CO·2, obtaining CO=1, so C=(-1,0). Also CO/OA=1/2, so 1/OA=1/2, obtaining OA=2, therefore A=(2,0), and the abscissa of point P is 2. The straight line passes through C=(-1,0) and D=(0,2), with slope k=2, so the straight line is y=2x+2. Point P is on the straight line and x=2, so P=(2,6). Point P is also on y=m/x, therefore 6=m/2, obtaining m=12, that is, the inverse proportional function is y=12/x. Comparing the two functions, when x>0, it is required that 2x+2≥12/x. Because x>0, both sides can be multiplied by x, obtaining 2x^2+2x-12≥0, that is, 2(x+3)(x-2)≥0. Combining with x>0, the solution is x≥2.
